title: Deciphering the clinical implication of an obesity-related gene signature as the novel biomarker for acute myocardial infarction diagnosis.
summary: Machine-learning feature selection on four GEO training expression datasets produced a five-gene obesity-related signature for acute myocardial infarction (IL1RN, TLR2, NFKBIA, MMP9 and ITLN1). Its reported AUC was 0.924 in the training analysis and 0.825 in the separate GSE59876 dataset; RT-qPCR also confirmed differential expression in AMI and control samples. These retrospective biomarker results do not establish prospective diagnostic benefit.
ai_technology: Machine-learning feature-gene selection using obesity-related genes and GEO expression data; the resulting signature was evaluated with ROC analysis. The article also used GSEA, CIBERSORT and ssGSEA for downstream analyses.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Four GEO expression datasets were used for training analyses and one for validation. The five-gene signature had AUC 0.924 and AUC 0.825 in GSE59876; RT-qPCR confirmed differential expression in AMI and control samples.
evidence.unknown: The GEO cohort analyses are retrospective; RT-qPCR confirms differential expression, not prospective diagnostic utility or improved patient outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection identified an obesity-related gene signature for AMI diagnosis; ROC analysis assessed its discrimination, while immune-infiltration analyses characterized associated patterns.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
